figures.finding: A minor is incapable of contracting: an obligation by a child under fourteen is null, and the same holds from fourteen to eighteen while the minor is under parental authority or has a curator, so the parents (as legal representatives) contract for the child; a minor of sixteen authorised by the parent by a public deed registered in the Civil Court may trade and is treated as of age for trade obligations; no share of earnings is set aside.

value.14to18: null while under parental authority or with a curator (art. 970); the parents act
value.tradeAuthorisation: parent's public deed registered in the Civil Court, First Hall (Commercial Code art. 9)

figures.applies: The Civil Code's rule reaches every contract, so writing, directing and producing deals as well as performing. No set-aside of a minor's earnings was found in the Civil Code or the Young Persons Regulations (blocker).

sources.said: The following persons are incapable of contracting, in the cases specified by law:  (a) minors;
Any obligation entered into by a child under the age … of fourteen years is also null.

The provisions of the last preceding article shall also … apply with regard to any person who has attained the age of … fourteen years, but has not attained the age of eighteen years, if … such person is subject to parental authority, or is provided with a … curator
A minor who has attained the age of sixteen years, may … trade and shall be deemed to be a major with regard to obligations … contracted by him for purposes of trade, if -

figures.finding: An employer must ask the Director (Employment and Industrial Relations) for written authorisation to employ a child under sixteen in cultural, artistic or advertising work, given case by case on a risk assessment and the Director of Education's no objection, with the Director's own conditions on hours, night work and rest never worse than those for light work (two hours on a school day and 12 a week in term; 7 hours a day and 35 a week in holidays to 15, 8 and 40 over 15; no work 8pm to 6am); from thirteen, activities the education minister approves need only a prior written notification; adolescents (16 to 18) at most 8 hours a day and 40 a week, not 10pm to 6am.

value.permit: written authorisation of the Director (DIER), case by case, with a risk assessment and the Director of Education's no objection (reg. 3(2))

figures.applies: The authorisation is for any 'employment of a child' in cultural or artistic activities, so a child employed as a writer or assistant on a production is reached as a performer is. The floor of conditions is the light-work schedule, which the Director may not undercut.

sources.said: An employer shall apply to the Director for written  authorisation to employ a child in cultural, artistic, sports or  advertising activities, and the Director may issue such  authorisation, in individual cases, for the employment of a child in  such activities:

thirteen years of age and the employment is for the  purposes of taking part in cultural, artistic, sports,  advertising or educational activities, approved by the  Minister responsible for education:

the Director may, at his discretion, attach such conditions as the Director deems fit on any issue relating to the conditions of employment of children, including on working time, night work, rest periods, and breaks
The working time for adolescents shall not exceed eight  hours a day and forty hours a week. … perform work between 8 p.m. on any one day and 6 a.m. of the … following day.
two hours on a school day and … 12 hours a week;

figures.finding: A minor not emancipated for trade may not be a company director or secretary; a minor of sixteen authorised to trade by the parent's registered deed is emancipated for trade.

value.exception: a minor of 16 or more emancipated for trade (Commercial Code art. 9)

figures.applies: From the Companies Act art. 142(1)(c) read with the Commercial Code art. 9 (my reading that the art. 9 authorisation is the emancipation for trade the Act names).

sources.said: A person shall not be qualified for appointment or to … hold office as director of a company or company secretary if: … (c) he is a minor who has not been emancipated for trade;
